title: Install crash recovery huddle - Oct 2028
body:
Context:
Quick huddle to capture the weird install failure we hit during the Zenith on-prem pilot (customer environment: Zenith Health cluster A). This is raw notes from the 30m recovery huddle and immediate follow-ups. Not a formal postmortem yet — intent is to capture actions, owners, and short-term mitigations so we can unblock the customer and adjust the runbook.

Attendees:
- Samira (install lead)
- Luca (networking)
- Marcus (SRE / provisioning)
- Priya (field eng, customer liaison)
- Kai (telemetry / observability)
- +1 on-call infra engineer (Ad-hoc)

Symptoms observed (timeline):
- 2028-10-11 04:12 UTC: First installer agent reported node provisioning timeout during PXE boot for node node-az1-07.
- 04:18 UTC: 5 additional nodes reported stalled NVMe init logs; OS installer retried and then failed.
- 04:33 UTC: Installer service crashed (oom?) on the bootstrap host; controller restarted. Customer stopped receiving progress updates.
- 04:40 UTC: Some nodes eventually booted with degraded IO performance; others remained offline (total 7/32 affected).

Immediate root-cause hypotheses (working):
1) Driver mismatch: The vendor-provided HBA driver on their hardware (MegaRAID 9820 variant) was not compatible with our packaged kernel module. The kernel attempted many retries during NVMe init, causing long hangs and increased memory usage on bootstrap host controllers that were polling remote node consoles.
2) PXE timeout amplification: A subtle change in the PXE server (customer infra) MTU and fragmentation caused multiple TFTP retransmits; installer agent retries are exponential and accumulate, causing controller thread saturation.
3) Telemetry blind spot: We did not have node-level early-boot kernel logs forwarded to the controller; inability to correlate kernel panics/driver messages made it take longer to identify HBA driver noise as the common pattern.

What we confirmed during huddle:
- Boot logs from node-az1-07 show repeated "nvme_core: timeout" and "raid: device not ready" messages between 04:05-04:20.
- Controller memory climbed from 6GB -> 14GB while handling concurrent stuck provisioning sessions (observed OOM kill of a helper process at 04:32).
- Customer's on-site infra team had recently bumped TFTP block size and changed network ACLs for management VLAN. Those changes correlate with a subset of nodes that failed behind the same ToR switch.

Short-term mitigations (actionable, owners, ETA):
- Rollback plan: Ask customer to revert TFTP blocksize to previous value (Priya owner). ETA: 2h. Expected to reduce PXE retransmits and allow clean reboots.
- Hotfix: Add an installer-agent flag to cap concurrent boot session threads to 8 on bootstrap controller to avoid OOM amplification (Marcus owner). Patch branch created: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2486 (ETA: 6h for canary patch + smoke).
- Driver workaround: Provide customers a one-off kernel package that includes the vendor HBA driver compiled against our installer kernel (Luca + customer infra). This is manual and risky; target nodes that failed only. (ETA: 24-48h after signoff).
- Observability: Force early-boot syslog capture to controller via temporary out-of-band SSH tunnel for the remaining failing nodes (Kai owner). This will let us confirm driver messages. (ETA: 3h).

Runbook gaps we identified (to address next sprint):
- Missing early-boot log ingestion: We need to ensure installer-agent collects kernel printk and early initrd logs to a staging bucket even if PXE/TFTP misbehaves. (Priority: High)
- Installer backpressure knobs: Default threads/concurrency for boot should be tunable by customer or auto-throttled when controller memory usage spikes. (Priority: Medium)
- Hardware compatibility matrix: We don't have a quick lookup for known HBA driver/firmware combos and recommended kernel packages. Add a "hardware-compat" checklist to runbook. (Priority: Medium)

Telemetry/observability asks (short):
- Kai: Add an alert when installer-controller RSS > 8GB for > 5m during active provisioning windows (INF-1293).
- Kai: Add a trace that tags nodes by ToR switch / management VLAN so we can detect correlated failures more quickly.
- Marcus: Enable short-term verbose logging for TFTP and PXE server on the bootstrap host during the re-run window (will increase noise).

Customer communication draft (Priya to send):
- Short note acknowledging impact, actions taken (rollback request, patch in flight), expected next steps and an ETA for blocked nodes. Include a safe rollback script and step-by-step for reverting TFTP change.

Open questions / unknowns: (Notes to self)
- Did the customer image builder also change the initramfs kernel? We need to diff boot artifacts across failing vs successful nodes.
- Are there NIC firmware combinations that interact badly with HBA retries? Check vendor KB.
- Is our retry logic for PXE/TFTP too aggressive in environments with management-network packet loss? Maybe add jitter/backoff.

Decision log during huddle:
- Do not proceed with broad kernel rebuild for all nodes (cost/risk) — only targeted nodes after confirming logs.
- Proceed with installer concurrency cap patch immediately to reduce blast radius.
- Customer to revert TFTP setting as fastest path to stability.

Immediate next steps (concrete owners & dates):
- Priya: Send rollback instructions to customer and request TFTP revert (by 2028-10-12 12:00 PT).
- Marcus: Push concurrency cap canary to a single bootstrap host and run a 2-node re-provision test (by 2028-10-12 EOD).
- Kai: Attach early-boot syslog forwarding for nodes node-az1-07 / node-az1-09 and upload logs to CONFLUENCE page (by 2028-10-12 15:00 PT).
- Luca: Start kernel driver compatibility check and vendor KB lookup; flag quick wins (by 2028-10-14).
- Samira: Draft postmortem skeleton and collect timestamps/logs for full analysis (by 2028-10-18).

Follow-ups to schedule:
- Cross-team retro with SRE/provisioning/networking in 1 week to decide permanent runbook changes and default limits.
- Product review: Think about making early-boot log collector an opt-out feature for private deployments (cost/retention implications).

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Reminder: Keep customer communication simple — avoid deep technical language until we have concrete root cause. They want an ETA.
- There's an open sales/legal thread about warranty around supported hardware for Private installs; loop in security/compliance if we end up shipping vendor drivers.

Attachments/Useful refs: (links in linked_artifacts)
- JIRA INF-1293 (controller memory OOM during provisioning)
- CONFLUENCE page: private-deploy/install-runbook-v2 (add runbook edits here)
- PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2486 (installer concurrency cap patch)

End notes (raw):
- This doc is intentionally raw. If you were in the huddle and have items to add, append below with initials and timestamp.
- If you are assigned an owner above and cannot meet the ETA, ping Samira and Priya in #deploys asap.
